newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LEEDS DROP BROLIN, RUSH AND THREE OTHERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEEDS DROP BROLIN, RUSH AND THREE OTHERS.

text.p: Leeds United have dropped five first team players, including Swede Tomas Brolin, from a tour of Sweden because manager George Graham has doubts about their future.
The Leeds clubcall line said Graham had decided to leave behind Welsh striker Ian Rush, Carlton Palmer, Tony Dorigo and Brian Deane as well as Brolin from the squad of 20 that departed on Tuesday.
It quoted Graham as saying that he felt Brolin had not committed himself long-term to the English premier league club's future.
He said the others were being left behind because there was no point taking them to Sweden if there were any doubts about their staying at Leeds.
Rush is likely to move on next season, Dorigo and Deane are out of contract and Palmer is unsettled.
Brolin, who was on loan to Parma, told the clubcall line however that he intended to stay at Leeds. "I'm staying here and working here. It's the only thing that I can do," he said.
